text.p: Lehman Brothers has raised the price target for Israel's Supersol Ltd and reiterated its outperform-rating in a report released on Tuesday.
Lehman said its new 12 month price target was 14-15 shekels, up from a previous 11 shekels per share.
Lehman maintained its 1997 earnings per share (EPS) estimate at 6.50 shekels, but it raised its 1998 EPS to 7.79 shekels from 7.29 shekels.

The report said the proceeds from the sale of Supersol's office supply business, Super Office, to competitor Office Depot, would not significantly affect Supersol's bottom line. But the sale is positive as it is "a long-awaited step in strenghtening the company's earnings momentum," the report said.

"We continue to view the shares an attractive investment opportunity. Trading at 19 times our 1997 EPS estimates and 16 times our 1998 estimates, we see continued opportunity for capital appreciation over the next 12 months as Supersol's growth rate accelerates next year."
Supersol closed at 12.29 shekels on Tuesday.
